extraction.name: IFEval
extraction.description: Instruction-Following Eval (IFEval) is a benchmark to evaluate the instruction-following ability of large language models using a set of prompts containing verifiable instructions. It contains 25 types of verifiable instructions and 541 prompts, with each prompt containing one or multiple verifiable instructions.
extraction.creator: Jeffrey Zhou, Tianjian Lu, Swaroop Mishra, Siddhartha Brahma, Sujoy Basu, Yi Luan, Denny Zhou, Le Hou
extraction.citeAs: Zhou, Jeffrey; Lu, Tianjian; Mishra, Swaroop; Brahma, Siddhartha; Basu, Sujoy; Luan, Yi; Zhou, Denny; Hou, Le. Instruction-Following Evaluation for Large Language Models. November 15, 2023.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The benchmark was constructed by identifying 25 types of verifiable instructions and creating 541 prompts containing one or more such instructions. Prompt creation used four steps: generating base prompts with one to three randomly selected verifiable instructions appended, using few-shot prompting to identify and remove illogical prompts, using another few-shot prompting approach to rephrase prompts for diversity, and then manually checking and editing the rephrased prompts one by one.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Software Collection, Manual Human Curator, Experiments
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw data are prompts synthesized from base prompts and appended verifiable instructions, then rephrased and manually edited. The released data include the prompts used for evaluation and code for verification.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Generated prompts were filtered to remove illogical prompts, rephrased to increase diversity of phrasing, and manually checked and edited. For evaluation, responses were also transformed under a loose criterion by removing markdown font modifiers, removing the first line, removing the last line, and combinations of these transformations.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Prompt synthesis involved appending one to three randomly selected verifiable instructions to base prompts, removing illogical prompts via few-shot prompting, rephrasing prompts via few-shot prompting, and manually checking and editing each prompt. For loose evaluation, each response was transformed using eight variants including identity, removing markdown modifiers, removing the first line, removing the last line, and combinations of these transformations.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The benchmark uses deterministic programmatic verification rather than human labeling. For a given response and verifiable instruction, a function determines whether the instruction is followed. The authors implemented relatively robust verification by considering commonly seen variations, and computed both strict and loose instruction-following accuracy.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The paper discusses false negatives in strict verification, such as markdown formatting causing naive string matching to fail. To address this, the authors define a loose accuracy criterion using transformed responses. They note that this reduces false negatives but may introduce false positives, so the loose criterion is considered a complement to the original criterion.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Simple heuristics and deterministic programming for instruction verification; few-shot prompting was used to identify illogical prompts and to rephrase prompts.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The authors release code and prompts used for evaluation at the GitHub repository. They state as future work that they plan to improve the prompts and verifiable instructions, make them more related to real-world applications, expand the approach with more verifiable instructions, and support multi-modal use cases.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The paper states that accurate instruction following is crucial not only for task precision but also for the safety and reliability of LLM implementations. Discrepancies or misunderstandings in following instructions can lead to unintended outputs, which might have dire results, especially in crucial scenarios like healthcare or autonomous systems.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The paper argues that human evaluation can lead to potential biases and inconsistencies for reproducibility, and that model-based evaluation can be biased or limited by the evaluator model. The proposed method is described as an easy-to-reproduce, unbiased, and automatic approach.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The paper notes that very few instructions are 100% verifiable objectively and automatically, and edge cases remain hard to determine. Strict verification can yield false negatives, while the loose criterion can introduce false positives. The current implementation can be improved by increasing the diversity and quantity of verifiable instructions and extending to multi-modal use cases.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is a benchmark for evaluating the instruction-following ability of large language models. It is used for automatic evaluation with prompt-level and instruction-level strict and loose accuracy metrics, for comparing models such as GPT-4 and PaLM 2, and for analyzing which instruction types are not usually followed.
